title: One copy hands off both the redlined picture and its spec list
goal: Handing a redline to a teammate takes two copies today: Copy Image for the picture, then Copy as Spec List for the text. When a document has measurements, Copy Image should put the spec list on the clipboard as text beside the picture, so pasting into a document or chat drops the picture and pasting into a plain text field drops the list, with nothing extra to learn.
notes: Open thread from the 2026-09-01 manager pass. Code: EditorState.copyCompositeToClipboard writes .png and .tiff only (Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift:546); copyMeasureSpecList already builds the text via MeasureSpecList.render(document:name:). NSPasteboard lets one item carry several types; declare the image types first so image-aware apps take them. Verify the paste order claim in real apps: some chat clients take the string when both exist, which is the thing to test before committing. Flag next-measure-panel; Current unchanged with the flag off.
acceptance: In the Next release with next-measure-panel on and at least one measurement: Copy Image (or the inspector Export section button), then paste into Notes or TextEdit, and the picture lands; paste into a plain text field (Spotlight, Terminal, a Safari address bar) and the spec list lands.

Pasting into Messages, Slack or Mail pastes the picture, not the text; this is checked by hand on at least two of them on the probe app before shipping. If any of them prefers the text, the change is withdrawn and a decision is opened with the observed behaviour instead.
A document with no measurements copies exactly what it copies today.

The Copied pill says what landed (picture, and the list when present); tests pin the pasteboard representations; Scripts/test.sh green; audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task.
